land.text: the Seleucid satrapy of the Erythraean Sea and Antiochia in Susiana, which Antiochus IV gave Hyspaosines to govern in 166/5 BC

predecessors.note: Characene page: 'Antiochus IV appointed Hyspaosines governor (eparch) of Antiochia and the Satrapy of the Erythraean Sea'; he 'declared independence as Parthian power approached' (infobox: established 141 BC).

land.text: Characene taken by Ardashir I: 'he invaded Characene State in the mouth of Tigris and took it' (Ardashir I page)

successors.note: Ardashir renamed the capital Astarabad-Ardashir (Charax Spasinu page); the area became known as Maysan.

capitals.name: Charax Spasinu (Alexandria, Antiochia, Jebel Khayabir near Naysan)
capitals.note: Charax Spasinu page, coordinates 30 53 41 N 47 34 41 E, on the Jabal Khuyabir tell near the confluence of the Karkheh and the Tigris. Founded by Alexander in 324 BC, rebuilt c. 166 BC under Antiochus IV, renamed for Hyspaosines; after 221-222 Astarabad-Ardashir.

correction.text: Characene at 'the head of the Persian Gulf, mostly in modern Iraq' around Charax Spasinu on the Tigris-Karkheh confluence, with Failaka and the coast of what today is Kuwait ('Hyspaosines founded the kingdom in what today is Kuwait', Tylos page)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (no Cliopatria row). Neither the Characene page nor the Hyspaosines page gives an area or boundary, so Basra and Maysan governorates plus Kuwait are the reading of the 'head of the Persian Gulf'. Babylonia (held in 127 BC) is an episode in the ledger, not part of the shape. The page also says the realm 'included Failaka and Bahrain' and that some scholars think it extended south of the Gulf (Meredates calls himself 'king of the Omani', c. 131), but dates neither: Bahrain and Oman are left out and noted.

ledger.note: 141 BC: Hyspaosines declares independence at the head of the Persian Gulf. Characene infobox 'Established 141 BC'; the Hyspaosines page: he 'declared independence in 141 BC' after Seleucid authority collapsed and passed to the Parthians. Other pages give 129 BC (Tylos) or 127 BC (Charax Spasinu, renaming the city) and the king list starts him c. 127 BC. The year is the page's; the modern units are the researcher's reading.

region.text: Babylon: 'Hyspaosines took advantage of the situation by seizing Babylon' (Hyspaosines page); the Parthian Empire page says Seleucia

ledger.note: 127 BC: Hyspaosines seizes Babylon from the Parthians. Hyspaosines page: 'Hyspaosines took advantage of the situation by seizing Babylon' and was recorded as king there; the Parthian Empire page says he 'invaded Babylonia and occupied Seleucia' in 127 BC. The page does not date the seizure inside 127.

region.text: Babylon: 'Hyspaosines took advantage of the situation by seizing Babylon' (Hyspaosines page); the Parthian Empire page says Seleucia

ledger.note: November 127 BC: the Parthian general Timarchus retakes Babylon, 'at the start of November 127 BC' (Hyspaosines page). The Parthian Empire page instead has Mithridates II forcing Hyspaosines out of Babylonia in 122 BC, two years after the Hyspaosines page has him dead (3-11 June 124 BC); the dated retaking is used.

region.text: Characene at 'the head of the Persian Gulf, mostly in modern Iraq' around Charax Spasinu on the Tigris-Karkheh confluence, with Failaka and the coast of what today is Kuwait ('Hyspaosines founded the kingdom in what today is Kuwait', Tylos page)

ledger.note: 124 BC: Hyspaosines accepts Parthian suzerainty and keeps ruling Characene as a vassal. Hyspaosines page (re-read 2026-10-19): 'In 124 BC, however, Hyspaosines accepted Parthian suzerainty, and continued to rule Characene as a vassal'; he fell ill on 3 June and died on 11 June 124 BC. The Characene page's infobox status is 'Autonomous state, frequently a vassal of the Parthian Empire', so the tint may lapse in the later centuries ('frequently'); no page dates a break, so one span -124 to 222 is the reading. Mirrors parthian-empire /ledger/21 (vassal_start characene), which has -122 (the Parthian Empire page's 'by 122 BC'); the Hyspaosines page dates it two years earlier. [Added after review me-06-x, 2026-10-19]

region.text: Characene at 'the head of the Persian Gulf, mostly in modern Iraq' around Charax Spasinu on the Tigris-Karkheh confluence, with Failaka and the coast of what today is Kuwait ('Hyspaosines founded the kingdom in what today is Kuwait', Tylos page)

ledger.note: 116 (the body of the Trajan page; its introduction and the Characene page say 115): Trajan sails down the Tigris to the Persian Gulf and 'received the submission of Athambelus, the ruler of Charax', a brief Roman client status for Characene (Parthian Empire page: Rome 'even subjugated Characene' in 115-116). The page gives no single year and no terms; the king keeps his throne (Attambelos VII, 113/14-117 in the king list), so this is a client tint over the standing Parthian suzerainty, not an annexation. Confidence 1: the year is bridged between 115 and 116. [Added after review me-06-x, 2026-10-19; Trajan's Parthian campaign page opened the same day]

ledger.note: 117: the Roman client status lapses with Trajan's withdrawal and death (the Trajan page: Hadrian 'relinquished Armenia, Mesopotamia, and Assyria'; a Palmyrene official at Charax 'shortly after Trajan's death' was appointed 'by a Parthian king of Charax', so the throne was still Characene's). The page does not date the end of the submission itself. [Added after review me-06-x, 2026-10-19]

ledger.note: 221/222: Ardashir I conquers Characene and the kingdom ends. Characene page: 'Ardashir's revolt established the Sasanian Empire'; infobox end 222; per later Arab histories he killed the last ruler (Abinergaos III, c. 210-222 in the king list). The Charax Spasinu page: 'In AD 221-222, Ardashir I defeated Characene forces' and renamed the capital Astarabad-Ardashir. The Ardashir I page gives no year for 'he invaded Characene State in the mouth of Tigris and took it'; the parthian-empire dossier ends the vassal tint in 224.

wars.name: Hyspaosines' invasion of Babylonia

zones.text: Babylon: 'Hyspaosines took advantage of the situation by seizing Babylon' (Hyspaosines page); the Parthian Empire page says Seleucia

wars.outcome: Hyspaosines held Babylon for part of 127 BC; Timarchus retook it at the start of November 127; in 124 BC Hyspaosines was forced to acknowledge Parthian suzerainty and died on 11 June 124.
wars.note: The Parthian Empire page adds that 'a Parthian attempt to conquer Characene had failed' earlier and that Mithridates II made the kings of Characene vassals by 122 BC.

wars.name: Trajan's Parthian campaign (Characene)
wars.outcome: Trajan reached Characene, where Attambelos VII ruled as a friend of Rome; Trajan withdrew in 117 (Parthian Empire page); the pages record no change of border.
wars.note: Characene page: 'In AD 115' Trajan conquered Mesopotamia and reached Characene (Attambelos VII reigns 113/14-117 in the king list). The Parthian Empire page says Rome 'even subjugated Characene' in 115-116. No border change is dated, so no zone. [Added after review me-06-x, 2026-10-19: the Trajan's Parthian campaign page says Trajan 'received the submission of Athambelus, the ruler of Charax' on his way to the Gulf (year 115 in its introduction, 116 in its body), recorded as a Roman client status in the ledger (vassal_start 116, vassal_end 117, confidence 1). The zones stay empty because no border moved.]

notes:
State Cliopatria lacks (new_slug characene), listed as needed by the me-06-a and me-06-c reports. Pages opened: Characene, Hyspaosines, Charax Spasinu (the 'Spasinou_Charax' title did not load), Parthian Empire, Tylos, Ardashir I.

DISAGREEMENTS BETWEEN PAGES: founding 141 BC (infobox, Hyspaosines) / 129 BC (Tylos) / 127 BC (Charax Spasinu, renaming of the city); Hyspaosines' recapture 'at the start of November 127 BC' (Hyspaosines) against 'forced out in 122 BC' (Parthian Empire; he died in 124 per the Hyspaosines page); Trajan 115 (Characene) against 115-116 (Parthian Empire); the Characene page calls the Sasanian founder 'Ardashir V' in one place. The parthian-empire dossier carries vassal_start characene at -122 and vassal_end at 224; the Characene page says Hyspaosines accepted Parthian suzerainty in 124 BC, and the conquest ended in 221-222.

LEFT OUT for want of a dated page: Bahrain (Tylos) and Failaka as parts of the realm (Failaka is inside the Kuwait country shape), Oman ('some scholars think the kingdom extended south of the Gulf'); the Tylos page says Characene ruled the island 'until the second century AD' and later Bahrain passed to the Sasanian province of Mazun, with no years. A gap-filler could open the Mazun page.

The king list (28 reigns, c. 127 BC to 222 AD) is on the Characene page; no rulers strip is entered because many reigns are given only as paired years (e.g. 95/94-90/89 BC). Gazetteer: all names resolve.
